newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS' OLAJUWON TO MISS A WEEK.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS' OLAJUWON TO MISS A WEEK.

text.p: Houston Rockets centre Hakeem Olajuwon was expected to be out of action for up to a week to recover from an irregular heartbeat that struck him at halftime of a Tuesday night game, the team said on Wednesday.

Physicians at Methodist Hospital had to administer an electric shock to Olajuwon's heart on Wednesday after medication failed to restore a normal heartbeart, Rockets spokesman Tim Frank said in a statement.
"He responded well and his heart went back into a normal cardiac rhythm...Hakeem is expected to be out of action for approximately five to seven days," he said.

Hospital spokeswoman Angela McPike told Reuters the All-Star centre was resting and would undergo a stress test early Thursday to check out the function of his heart. It was likely he would be released from the hospital shortly after the test, she said.
Olajuwon, 33, was sent to Methodist Hospital, one of the nation's leading heart treatment centres, after suffering the heart problem during halftime of a game with the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Frank said Olajuwon reported "a little jumpiness in his chest" after having a drink of water during the break. Team doctors sent him by ambulance to the hospital after an examination revealed the unusual heartbeat.

Television reports showed Olajuwon emerging from the ambulance and walking under his own power into the hospital. He had played 18 minutes and scored 10 points in first half of the game, which the Rockets eventually won 122-93.
Olajuwon missed six games in 1991 when he experienced the same problem. At that time, medication also failed to restore a normal heartbeat and he was given a shock to his heart, team officials said.
Frank said team officials were not in a "panic" about Olajuwon or his future, but said, "It could happen to him again down the road."

Teammate Clyde Drexler told reporters he was worried about his long-time friend. "I'm very concerned. Anytime anyone has something of that magnitude you have to be concerned about their health, first and foremost."

Olajuwon, a native of Nigeria but now a U.S. citizen, led the Rockets to National Basketball Association championships in 1993-94 and 1994-95 and was a member of the U.S. Dream Team in the Summer Olympics this year.
